description:
About Dell Technologies 
 
At Dell Technologies, we believe technology is essential for human progress. We're committed to transforming lives everywhere — and our Services Operations organization is at the forefront of that transformation internally, reimagining how we work by embedding AI powered agents to automate, accelerate, and enhance business outcomes across the enterprise.
About the Role
We are scaling an agentic AI program across multiple operations domains, with a workflow pipeline that extends over the next several fiscal years. Hundreds of automation ready workflows have already been identified across the organization. What we need now are people who can sit with a team, learn how the work actually happens, translate that into a specification an engineer can build against, build most of it themselves, and carry it through architecture and security review into production — where someone uses it every day.  That is this job.
As a Forward Deployed AI Engineer, you will split your time between hands on engineering (~60%) and program management (~40%). You will not work from a backlog someone hands you. Instead, you embed directly with domain teams — joining their meetings, examining their queues and exception reports — and leave with a scoped agent, a spec, and a working prototype. Then you stay long enough to confirm the team actually changed how they work, because an agent nobody uses is a failed agent, no matter how well it was engineered.
This role is deliberately two sided: you will write real code and you will help build the program discipline that lets dozens of agents ship without chaos. If you want to do only one of those, this is not the right fit.
 Key Responsibilities 
 
Build Agents & Enabling Capabilities (~75% of your time)
•    Embed with operations teams and stakeholder to map how work truly gets done today. Identify the exceptions, workarounds, and judgment calls — because that is where agents succeed or fail.
•    Translate messy workflows into clear agent specifications: scope and boundaries, required tools and data, guardrails, human in the loop checkpoints, and explicit success criteria.
•    Build and prototype quickly. Put working software in front of real users early, then harden what survives contact. You are expected to write the code with AI assistance, not just describe it.
•    Design the evaluation before you design the agent. Define how you will know the agent or enabling technology is right, instrument it, and measure it against real cases — not happypath demos.
•    Own the path to production: IT architecture review, security and governance approvals, controlled rollout with human review, and production observability.
•    Debug agents and other technology in production. Trace failures to root cause, tune prompts, tools, and retrieval, and fix the underlying problem rather than papering over it.
Build the Services Agentic AI Acceleration PMO (~25% of your time)
•    Maintain the portfolio tracker with accuracy: every agent and technology stage, owner, status, and planned versus actual dates. Ensure the right milestones, actions, and gates are captured and tracked.
•    Run intake with domain teams, stake holders and the team lead: help them turn rough ideas into scoped, scored, and sequenced candidates that can pass a review board.
•    Author the specs, templates, and how-to guides that enable other pods to build agents independently.
•    Prepare portfolio and status reporting for senior leadership, including executive level materials. You will be asked to explain a red status to someone senior — along with your plan to get well.
•    Steward the stage gate process so agents and enabling technology advance on evidence, not optimism.
•    Identify patterns. When three domains ask for the same capability, turn it into a reusable component instead of a third one-off.
 
 What Success Looks Like 
 
•    First 90 days: You are embedded with one domain team and can explain their workflow better than most people in it. One agent is specified and prototyped, and you know the tracker and gate process well enough to run it yourself.
•    By 6 months: At least one agent and/or enabling capability you built is in production and actively used, with evaluation and monitoring in place. You are running intake for a domain and preparing portfolio reporting with light review.
•    By 12 months: Multiple agents and enablers are delivered across more than one domain. Teams request you by name. Something you standardized — a template, a component, a spec pattern — is being used by pods you never worked with directly.
Required Qualifications
•    2–3 years of professional experience in software engineering, data science, applied ML, or technical consulting. Exceptional recent graduates with substantial internship, coop, or research experience will be considered.
•    Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, or a related field — or equivalent practical experience.
•    Strong Python skills. You can read an unfamiliar codebase, extend it, and leave it better than you found it.
•    Handson experience building with large language models: prompting, tool and function calling, retrieval, and chaining multiple steps into reliable workflows.
•    Ability to write a technical specification a peer could build from without a meeting.
•    Comfort working directly with technical and non-technical business stakeholders. You can run a working session — not just attend one — and you can disagree with a senior person respectfully and with evidence.
•    Demonstrated ownership of something end to end: shipped, used by real people, and supported after launch.
Preferred Qualifications
We do not expect a candidate at this level to have all of these. Depth in two or three is a strong signal.
•    Exposure to AI development platforms and assistants such as DataRobot, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, or comparable tools.
•    Familiarity with agent design patterns: orchestration, agent to agent handoff, human in the loop review, and failure/fallback handling.
•    Evaluation and observability for LLM systems — building eval sets, tracing, regression testing prompts, and monitoring quality in production.
•    Enterprise deployment experience: architecture review, security and data governance, controlled rollouts, and change management.
•    Background in operations, services, supply chain, or another process heavy business function.
•    Program or delivery tooling experience: Jira, Confluence, stage gate delivery, portfolio tracking, and executive reporting.
•    Frontend or automation skills for internal tools (light web apps, dashboards, or workbook automation).
Our Environment
You will work with DataRobot, Windsurf, GitLab, Copilot, and other AI development tools alongside internal platforms and data sources. Program governance runs through Confluence and a portfolio tracker, with formal architecture and security review gates before anything reaches production. Expect a real enterprise environment: approvals, controls, and legacy systems are part of the job — not an obstacle to route around.
Who Thrives in This Role
•    High agency. You are given a domain and an outcome, not a task list. You decide what to do on Monday.
•    Bias toward working software. You would rather show a rough prototype in week one than a polished document in week three.
•    Comfortable not being the expert. You will be the least knowledgeable person in the room about the business process, and you will ask questions until you are not.
•    Writes clearly. Specs, updates, and executive summaries are a real part of the job.
•    Finishes. The last 20% — the rollout, the training, the monitoring, and the adoption — is the part that ultimately determines success.
 
 Compensation 

Dell is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. The salary range for this position is $91,800 - $118,800. Actual offers may vary based on relevant skills, experience, and geographic location. This role is also eligible for Dell's comprehensive benefits package, including incentive plans, medical, vision, and dental coverage, 401(k), paid time off, and more.
 
 Why Join Dell Technologies 

•    Work at the intersection of AI and real world enterprise operations at scale.
•    Be part of a program with executive visibility and direct business impact.
•    Access cutting edge AI tools and platforms as part of your daily work.
•    Grow your career within a Fortune 50 technology leader committed to innovation, inclusion, and your development.
 Dell Technologies is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.
